stories.title: Spain asks EU for help to process 5,000 Ceuta migrants amid local unrest
stories.summary: Thousands of migrants remain in the Spanish enclave, triggering anger among Ceuta residents. Spain has asked Europe’s Border and Coastguard Agency, Frontex, for help to process some 5,000 migrants in Ceuta who crossed into the North African territory one month ago. Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska sent the request to Beate Gminder, the European Commission’s director general for migration and home affairs, on Friday. Grande-Marlaska also requested an extra 10 Frontex officers to speed up screening efforts. Spanish authorities must identify those remaining in Ceuta to establish whether they are entitled to international protection or, if not, begin procedures for their return. Authorities say between 5,000 and 8,000 migrants, including unaccompanied children, still in Ceuta are among the 72,000 people who crossed the border from Morocco on July 30. The rush killed 82 people on the Spanish side of the border and 14 on the Moroccan side, according to official numbers. Human rights groups reported higher figures. Spain’s request comes amid rising tensions in Ceuta, after a series of protests by residents who have demanded the migrants leave. Tents on Trampolin Beach, where many migrants have been camping, have been attacked and set on fire. Twelve migrants were arrested on Thursday after stoning an army vehicle, injuring one soldier and four migrants. Eleven were expelled from Ceuta, El Pais newspaper reported on Friday, citing sources from the city’s main court.

stories.title: Underground missile shelter to be built near Tokyo Station
stories.summary: Tokyo plans to convert an underground parking facility near Tokyo Station into a ballistic missile shelter with blast-proof doors and emergency supplies. The shelter project responds to North Korea’s missile threats and aims to protect residents and tourists. The central government announced in 2025 it plans to set up similar shelters in remote islands in the southern prefecture of Okinawa. The Tokyo metropolitan government has unveiled a plan to use an underground facility near Tokyo Station as a shelter for residents and tourists in the event of a ballistic missile attack. Tokyo Governor Yuriko Koike told a press conference earlier in August that a survey will begin in the current fiscal year through March in preparation for revamping Yaesu Parking Lot, which is located about 2m to 11m underground. The alterations are expected to include setting up blast-proof doors and storage shelves for emergency supplies, a metropolitan government official said. The facility has a total floor space of roughly 13,000 sq. It would be the capital city’s second emergency underground shelter, with a 1,400 sq m storage facility for disasters at Azabu-Juban subway station currently under conversion, the official said. Koike said that the Yaesu parking facility was chosen for its proximity to Tokyo Station, which she described as “the gateway to the capital” with many visiting the area. The plan comes as North Korea has repeatedly test-fired ballistic missiles into regional waters, including the Sea of Japan, also known as East Sea, in recent years while advancing its nuclear development programme. Koike described the neighboring country’s repeated missile launches as “a serious and grave threat that can never be tolerated” and stressed the need to “protect the lives and property of Tokyo residents” from attacks. The completion date, specific construction requirements and costs of the project will be determined after the survey, which is slated to continue into fiscal 2027, according to the official.

stories.title: Inside Thailand’s bid to wire the world’s AI revolution
stories.summary: In the rush to build an AI future, semiconductors are the silicon rock stars that soak up all the applause. Yet behind the curtain, an unglamorous stagehand is doing much of the heavy lifting. Printed circuit boards (PCBs) are the copper-laced panels inside every mobile phone, car key fob, digital camera and data-centre server rack on Earth.
